text.p: British pay television operator BSkyB said Friday that its first-quarter pre-tax profits rose 31 percent to 66 million pounds ($107.5 million).
The company, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the leading shareholder, said total paying subscribers reached 5.65 million in September, a net increase for the quarter of 146,000.
"The company has performed strongly in the first quarter and has achieved significant growth in both revenue and profits," said BSkyB Chief Executive Sam Chisholm.
"Our increased investment in all areas of programming and the quality and choice we offer our subscribers will maintain our impetus," he added.
Operating revenues for the three months to Sept. 30 increased to 266 million pounds ($433 million), a rise of 24 percent.

BSkyB has said it plans to introduce digital satellite broadcasting into Britain late next year. Pay-per-view sports events and movies are likely to be one of the prime sources of income from the extra channels provided by digital.
BSkyB said it would show its second pay-per-view event on Nov. 9 when Mike Tyson and Evander Holyfield meet in Las Vegas for the WBA Heavyweight Boxing crown.
However, Friday's planned launch of WBTV-The Warner Channel was postponed Thursday evening.

The Warner Channel -- a mixture of Bugs Bunny cartoons and vintage movies -- was apparently a victim of the legal battle being fought in the United States between Murdoch and the combined might of CNN founder Ted Turner and Time Warner.

That clash of the titans centres on whether Time Warner, the second-largest U.S. cable operator, will carry News Corp's 24-hour Fox News Service in New York City. Fox is a major rival to CNN, now part of Time Warner following a recent merger.
